newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian value stocks beat growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian value stocks beat growth in 1996.

text.p: Australian listed companies classed as value stocks by investment consultant Frank Russell Co Pty Ltd significantly outperformed those classed as growth stocks in the 1996 calendar year, the consultancy said on Monday.
"Growth stocks led value stocks in the early part of 1996, buoyed by the performance of a number of media and mining stocks, but stalled midyear," Frank Russell Co said.
"By year end value stocks had returned 21.64 percent versus a growth stocks return of 5.67 percent as measured by the ASX/Russell All Value and the ASX/Russell All Growth indexes."

The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX)/Russell style indexes were introduced by the ASX in June last year and are based on three existing ASX indexes -- the All Ordinaries, the ASX 100 and the Small Ordinaries.
The stocks within these indexes have been split into growth and value components to create six new indexes which separately track their performance.
Style analysis was developed in the 1970s as a way of explaining the different approaches fund managers take to evaluating securities.

Russell's model of stock returns splits the investment decision into two key factors - firstly, the company's size and secondly, whether its stock is attractive due to its earnings growth, or because of its relative value.

Analysis of ASX/Russell indexes show that value stocks have outperformed growth stocks every year since 1991, when the indexes were established. During this period, value stocks also have shown lower volatility than growth stocks.
"This year, value's dominance of growth was evident at both the large and small capitalisation ends of the market," said Peter Gunning, research analyst for Frank Russell Co.

"In a year when small companies as defined by ASX Small Ordinaries Index significantly outperformed large stocks defined by the ASX 100 Index (28.28 percent versus 12.65 percent), value stocks outperformed their growth counterparts across the full range of capitalisation," Gunning said.

ASX/Russell indexes are reconstituted annually to reflect changes in the market. This reconstitution is based on changes to the relative rankings of each security's price to net tangible assets (P/NTA) ratio in the ASX All Ordinaries Index.
Securities with higher P/NTA ratios are classed as growth stocks while stocks with lower P/NTA ratios are classed as value.
